result.summary: This PR fixes undefined behavior in CBloomFilter's sizing calculations: division by zero when nElements is 0, and float-to-unsigned-int conversion that is UB for NaN, infinity, negative values, or values outside the unsigned range. It requires false-positive rates to be in [0,1], preserves the existing empty match-all-state for zero elements, uses the max permitted filter size for a zero rate, and clamps the size in floating point before converting to an integer. It adds unit tests covering these boundaries and updates the fuzz harness to exercise the full valid rate and element-count ranges instead of avoiding the problematic inputs.
result.problem: The four-argument CBloomFilter constructor, used only by tests and the fuzz target today, invokes undefined behavior for a range of inputs (zero elements causing division by zero, invalid or extreme false-positive rates causing invalid float-to-int conversions). This produces UB that sanitizers or fuzzers can flag, obscuring real bugs and leaving the calculation formally unsafe if the constructor is ever used more broadly.

result.card: This PR fixes undefined behavior in CBloomFilter's sizing math: division by zero for zero elements, and float-to-unsigned-int conversion that is UB for NaN, infinity, negative values, or out-of-range finite values. The affected four-argument constructor is currently exercised only by unit tests and the fuzz target, per the author, so the fix mainly improves test/fuzz signal quality and hardens shared bloom-filter code rather than closing a live production bug. The PR adds targeted unit tests for the boundary cases and rewrites the fuzz harness to cover the full valid rate and element-count ranges.
